From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 calibration kickoff — draft matrix attached

Team —

Agenda for our calibration thread this week (tactical):
- Confirm band distributions across Eng/Product for Q3 cycles
- Resolve 5 borderline ratings flagged by managers
- Agree on any band realignment that impacts compensation or promotion eligibility

Attached is a first-pass calibration matrix and a short PDF with anonymized borderline examples. Please review the examples before you propose swaps — they include manager notes and signal sources (OKRs, peer feedback, missed deadlines).

Quick asks:
- Connor: can you run the distribution broken out by team overlaps (Backend, Platform) and drop the numbers into the matrix?
- Vivek: flag any cases where a swap would materially change a promotional pipeline (we should avoid surprise escalations to execs)
- Laura/Stephanie: is HR sign-off required for any >1-band adjustments?

Target: finalize by end of week so comp ops can prepare statements.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, People & Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- calibration-matrix-draft-2026Q3.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)
- anonymized-borderline-examples.pdf (PDF)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 calibration kickoff — draft matrix attached

Marissa —

I looked through the anonymized examples. Two quick notes:
1) Example #3 (Platform IC, borderline) has a strong peer signal but weak delivery in the last sprint — manager is proposing a 3 -> 4. I agree with the manager on trajectory, but promotion eligibility looks marginal given comp cycle timing.
2) Example #5 overlaps across Backend and Platform — both managers put them at the cusp. If we swap the higher rating to Backend, Platform loses a headcount that feeds our infra roadmap next quarter.

Proposal: instead of a direct swap, apply a constrained curve adjustment: move one person up a rating but reserve a development plan + checkpoint in 6 weeks. That minimizes retroactive comp changes and gives the person a clear improvement window.

If we go this route we need HR to confirm whether a 1-band adjustment with a documented development checkpoint is acceptable without exec approval.

-Vivek
VP Eng

Thanks — I pulled the distribution by team and updated the attached sheet (tab: team-distribution). Highlights:
- Backend and Platform both have a slightly higher density in the upper-middle band compared to last cycle (+2.1% and +1.8%).
- The 5 borderline cases are concentrated in two pods that ship across both areas.

On the specific swap Vivek called out: the individual under consideration (anonymized as BLD-5) has two recent OKR wins that are strong but also one missed delivery tied to a dependency outside their control. My read: trajectory supports a 3->4 but we should pair that with a timeboxed success metric to avoid retrospective objections.

I attached an "anonymized-borderline-examples.pdf" export I prepared with manager notes redacted for cross-check. If people agree on the constrained-adjustment pattern, I can add a short language block to the matrix that captures the 6-week checkpoint and metrics.

Next steps I propose:
1) We agree the constrained-adjustment pattern as our default for borderline swaps that affect promotion pipelines.
2) HR confirms whether that pattern triggers a formal sign-off or just comp ops notification.
3) Stephanie to capture the final decisions and owner list for communication to managers.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Platform
Redwood Inference

Connor/Vivek/Marissa —

From an HR compliance perspective: a 1-band adjustment paired with a documented development checkpoint is typically handled as a managers' decision with HR notified. Anything that changes comp retroactively or a >1-band move requires HR and People Leadership sign-off.

Concrete language I'd recommend adding to the matrix (short form):
"Constrained Adjustment: provisional 1-band increase tied to documented 6-week success metrics. HR to be notified; escalation to People Leadership required for >1-band changes or retroactive comp adjustments."

If you want, I can provide a short note template managers can use when they communicate the checkpoint to the IC.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, People Ops
Redwood Inference

2) Any template language you recommend we share with managers for the checkpoint?
